'''Busch Series''': 2 }} '''Haas CNC Racing''' was an American professional [[stock car racing]] team that competed in the [[NASCAR Sprint Cup Series]] and [[NASCAR Busch Series]]. Founded in 2002 by [[Gene Haas]], the founder of [[Haas Automation]], the team was established after Haas—then a sponsor of [[Hendrick Motorsports]]—decided to start his own operation. The team ceased operations after the 2008 season, merging into [[Stewart–Haas Racing]] when three-time NASCAR champion [[Tony Stewart]] joined as a driver and acquired a 50% ownership stake. The team was based and headquartered in [[Kannapolis, North Carolina]] – roughly 10 miles (16 km) north of [[Charlotte Motor Speedway]] – alongside sister team and [[Formula One]] entrant [[Haas F1 Team]]. ==History== After years as an associate sponsor of [[Hendrick Motorsports]],{{cite web |date=June 1, 2002 |title=NASCAR Driver Jack Sprague - Interview |url=http://www.stockcarracing.com/featurestories/scrp_0206_nascar_driver_jack_sprague/viewall.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326092456/http://www.stockcarracing.com/featurestories/scrp_0206_nascar_driver_jack_sprague/ |archive-date=March 26, 2016 |access-date=May 2, 2015 |website=[[TEN: The Enthusiast Network|stockcarracing.com]] |publisher=[[TEN: The Enthusiast Network]]}} [[Gene Haas]] announced in April 2002 that he would start his own [[Winston Cup]] team for the [[2003 NASCAR Winston Cup Series|2003 season]]. Hendrick agreed to supply cars, engines, and technical support. Haas signed [[Jack Sprague]]—who had spent six years driving in the Busch and Craftsman Truck Series for Hendrick—as the team's driver. Sprague brought his [[NetZero]] sponsorship with him, and the car was designated to No. 0.{{cite web |author1=Haas CNC Racing |date=April 19, 2002 |title=Haas Automation, Jack Sprague announce new Dissatisfied with [[Joe Gibbs Racing]]’s switch from [[Chevrolet]] to [[Toyota]], Stewart wanted to return to racing with Chevrolet. Meanwhile, team owner Haas sought Stewart’s star power to attract sponsors and talent. The team was ultimately shut down and merged into [[Stewart–Haas Racing]].{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2008 |title=Tony Stewart to partner with Haas Racing in 2009 |url=http://www.racewayreport.com/news/stewart_haas_racing.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222000020/http://www.racewayreport.com/news/stewart_haas_racing.html |archive-date=2025-02-22 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=www.racewayreport.com |language=en }}{{cite news |date=July 11, 2008 |title=Fifty Percent Ownership Was Key To Stewart's Deal With Haas CNC |url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Daily/Issues/2008/07/Issue-203/Sponsorships-Advertising-Marketing/Fifty-Percent-Ownership-Was-Key-To-Stewarts-Deal-With-Haas-CNC.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220175011/http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Daily/Issues/2008/07/Issue-203/Sponsorships-Advertising-Marketing/Fifty-Percent-Ownership-Was-Key-To-Stewarts-Deal-With-Haas-CNC.aspx |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=11 December 2016 |work=[[SportsBusiness Daily]]}}{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Marty |date=July 9, 2008 |title=Stewart granted release from Gibbs, will move to Haas |url=https://www.espn.com/racing/nascar/cup/news/story?id=3479199 |access-date=11 December 2016 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |location=[[Charlotte, North Carolina]]}} == Sprint Cup Series == === Car No. 66 history === ; Jack Sprague and Multiple Drivers (2002–2003) The No. 0 car, sponsored by [[NetZero]] and driven by [[Jack Sprague]], debuted as a Pontiac under Haas in 2003. Sprague opened the season with a career-best 14th-place finish at the [[2003 Daytona 500|Daytona 500]],{{cite web |date=July 16, 2003 |title=Sprague/Haas CNC Racing part ways |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/sprague-haas-cnc-racing-part-ways/?v=2&s=1&q=Jack+Sprague+2003 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705040132/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/sprague-haas-cnc-racing-part-ways/?v=2&s=1&q=Jack+Sprague+2003 |archive-date=5 July 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015 |website=[[Motorsport.com]] |publisher=motorsport.com |location=[[Harrisburg, North Carolina]]}} but the team soon began to struggle. After a 40th-place finish at [[Overton's 400|Chicagoland]], Sprague was released and replaced by [[John Andretti]],{{cite news |date=July 16, 2003 |title=Haas names Andretti to drive at Loudon |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/haas-names-andretti-to-drive-at-loudon/?s=1&q=haas+cnc+pontiac |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220153237/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/haas-names-andretti-to-drive-at-loudon/?s=1&q=haas+cnc+pontiac |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=11 December 2016 |work=[[Motorsport.com]] |location=[[Harrisburg, North Carolina]]}} who finished 41st at [[2003 New England 300|New Hampshire]] and 33rd at [[Gander Outdoors 400|Pocono]], before qualifying 15th and finishing 19th at [[Go Bowling at The Glen|Watkins Glen]]. Due to Andretti’s prior commitment with [[Dale Earnhardt, Inc.]], [[Jason Leffler]] drove the car at the [[2003 Brickyard 400|Brickyard 400]], finishing 33rd. Although Leffler lost his ride in the No. 2 truck for [[Ultra Motorsports]] in the [[NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series]] because of that start, Haas soon hired him as the team’s full-time driver.{{cite news |date=August 28, 2003 |title=Leffler named driver No. 0 rest of season |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/leffler-named-driver-no-0-rest-of-season/?s=1&q=haas+cnc+pontiac |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220153239/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/leffler-named-driver-no-0-rest-of-season/?s=1&q=haas+cnc+pontiac |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=11 December 2016 |work=[[Motorsport.com]] |location=[[Harrisburg, North Carolina]]}} ;Ward Burton (2003–2004) [[File:Nascarphx13.jpg|left|thumb|2004 No. 0 NetZero Chevrolet]] [[Ward Burton]] took over driving duties late in the 2003 season after eight years with [[Bill Davis Racing]],{{cite web |date=October 9, 2003 |title=Ward Burton moves to Haas CNC in 2004 |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/ward-burton-moves-to-haas-cnc-in-2004/?v=2&s=1&q=Ward+Burton+2004 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705001042/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/ward-burton-moves-to-haas-cnc-in-2004/?v=2&s=1&q=Ward+Burton+2004 |archive-date=5 July 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015 |website=motorsport.com |location=[[Huntersville, North Carolina]]}} while [[Jason Leffler]] moved to the [[Busch Series]] to drive the No. 00 car. Burton's best finishes in the final four races were 13th at [[Atlanta Motor Speedway|Atlanta]] and 18th at [[Rockingham Speedway|Rockingham]]. In the [[2004 NASCAR Nextel Cup Series|2004]] off-season, Pontiac exited NASCAR, prompting the team to switch back to [[Chevrolet]]. Burton started the year with a 17th-place finish at the [[2004 Daytona 500|Daytona 500]] and followed it with a 9th at [[2004 Subway 400|Rockingham]], putting the team 9th in points. Despite two top-20s in the next three races, the team began to slide. A 10th-place run at [[2004 Auto Club 500|California]] broke the slump, followed by five consecutive top-20 finishes. Burton earned an outside pole at the [[2004 Brickyard 400|Brickyard 400]] but crashed early, finishing 39th. He scored another 10th-place finish at [[1000Bulbs.com 500|Talladega]] in October but ended up 40th at [[Can-Am 500|Phoenix]]. ;Mike Bliss (2004–2005) Burton was soon replaced by [[2002 NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series]] champion [[Mike Bliss]],{{cite news |date=November 9, 2004 |title=Bliss Replaces Burton At Haas/CNC |url=http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2004/11/Bliss-Replaces-Burton-At-Haascnc.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220144134/http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2004/11/Bliss-Replaces-Burton-At-Haascnc.aspx |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=17 December 2016 |work=[[Motor Racing Network]]}} who debuted with a 10th-place finish at [[2004 Mountain Dew Southern 500|Darlington]] and was signed for the [[2005 NASCAR Nextel Cup Series|2005 season]].{{cite news |date=December 11, 2004 |title=Hass Tabs Bliss |url=http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2004/12/Hass-Tabs-Bliss.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220142620/http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2004/12/Hass-Tabs-Bliss.aspx |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=17 December 2016 |work=[[Motor Racing Network]]}} That year, [[Best Buy]] joined as an associate and four-race primary sponsor,{{cite news |date=January 25, 2005 |title=Best Buy Teams With Haas |url=http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2005/01/Best-Buy-Teams-With-Haas.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220141106/http://www.mrn.com/Race-Series/NASCAR-Sprint-Cup/News/Articles/2005/01/Best-Buy-Teams-With-Haas.aspx |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=17 December 2016 |work=[[Motor Racing Network]] |location=[[Harrisburg, North Carolina]]}} with the [[United States Coast Guard|U.S. Coast Guard]] backing one race. Bliss started the season with four consecutive 18th-place finishes and later posted top-10s at [[Pocono 400|Pocono]] (9th) and [[Bass Pro Shops Night Race|Bristol]] (7th), but was released at season's end. ;Jeff Green (2006–2007) For [[2006 NASCAR Nextel Cup Series|2006]] [[Jeff Green (racing driver)|Jeff Green]] replaced [[Mike Bliss]] as the driver. [[Best Buy]] became the primary sponsor, taking over after [[NetZero]]'s departure. The car number was changed to 66 in honor of the year Best Buy opened its first store in 1966.{{Cite web |last=Release |first=Team Press |title=NASCAR.COM - Best Buy on board with Green's No. 66 - Jan 12, 2006 |url=http://www.nascar.com/2006/news/headlines/cup/01/12/jgreen_bestbuy/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628232752/http://www.nascar.com/2006/news/headlines/cup/01/12/jgreen_bestbuy/index.html |archive-date=2011-06-28 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.nascar.com |language=en |url-status=live }} Green finished 28th in the 2006 standings and was re-signed for the [[2007 NASCAR Nextel Cup Series|2007 season]]. However, on October 22, 2007, it was announced that [[Jeremy Mayfield]] would replace Green for the final four races of the year. Following the season, Best Buy left to sponsor [[Elliott Sadler]]’s No. 19 Dodge at [[Gillett Evernham Motorsports]]. [[File:EM_P1020818_(2412669876).jpg|right|thumb|[[Scott Riggs]] in the No. 66 at [[Las Vegas Motor Speedway]] in 2008]] ;Scott Riggs (2008) In 2008, former Evernham driver [[Scott Riggs]] took over the No. 66 car, bringing sponsorship from State Water Heaters after moving from [[Morgan–McClure Motorsports]]. Additional sponsors included [[Hunt Brothers Pizza]] and [[Haas Automation]]. Although Riggs initially struggled, his performance improved following the mid-summer announcement that [[Tony Stewart]] would become the team's new co-owner. Riggs finished the season inside the top 35 in points but was ultimately released in favor of [[Ryan Newman (racing driver)|Ryan Newman]], who had recently left [[NASCAR operations of Team Penske|Penske Racing]] to join the newly formed [[Stewart–Haas Racing]] team. ==== Car No. 66 results ==== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; font-size:75%" ! {{small|35}} | colspan=20| |} === Car No. 70 history === ;Multiple Drivers (2002–2004) The No. 60 car debuted in 2002 as a fifth entry for [[Hendrick Motorsports]], with [[Gene Haas]] listed as the owner. [[Jack Sprague]], Hendrick's Busch Series driver, attempted six races (qualifying for three) to prepare for a full-time run with Haas. His best finish was 30th at the season finale in [[Homestead–Miami Speedway|Homestead–Miami]].{{cite web |date=November 17, 2002 |title=Homestead: Jack Sprague race report |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/homestead-jack-sprague-race-report/?v=2&s=1&q=Jack+Sprague+2003 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705015831/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/homestead-jack-sprague-race-report/?v=2&s=1&q=Jack+Sprague+2003 |archive-date=5 July 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015 |website=motorsport.com |location=[[Homestead, Florida]]}} In 2003, while Sprague and Haas ran the No. 0 Pontiac full-time, the No. 60 Chevy returned under the Hendrick banner with [[David Green (racing driver)|David Green]]. Sponsored by [[Haas Automation]], with support from [[Kellogg's]] and [[NetZero]], the team initially targeted restrictor plate races. They failed to qualify for the first two, then finished 32nd at Daytona and 35th at Talladega, running full NetZero branding after the No. 0 car missed the field.{{cite web |date=September 29, 2003 |title=Talladega II: Green/Leffler race report |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-cup/news/talladega-ii-green-leffler-race-report/?v=2&s=1&q=David+Green+2003 |url-status=dead |access-date=13 May 2015 |website=motorsport.com |location=[[Huntersville, North Carolina]]}} Later that year, [[Brian Vickers]] made his Cup debut in the No. 60 at Charlotte, qualifying 20th and Sauter]] in the No. 70 in 2007.]] ;Johnny Sauter (2006–2007) The No. 70 car made its debut as the second Haas entry at the [[2006 Coca-Cola 600]], driven by [[Johnny Sauter]]. He ran in the top 10 for most of the race before a blown tire caused him to crash. The team made another attempt later that season at the [[2006 Brickyard 400|Brickyard 400]] but failed to qualify. In 2007, it was announced that the No. 70 would compete full-time, with Sauter and sponsor [[Yellow Transportation]] moving up from the [[Busch Series]]. After the first five races, Sauter and the team worked their way into the top 35 in Owner's Points—securing a guaranteed starting spot—but missed the [[2007 Food City 500|Food City 500]] at [[Bristol Motor Speedway|Bristol]]. Despite that setback, they earned top-10 finishes at 9th in the [[2007 Subway Fresh Fit 500|Subway Fresh Fit 500]] and 5th in the [[2007 Chevy Rock & Roll 400|Chevy Rock & Roll 400]]. ;Multiple drivers (2008) In 2008, [[Jeremy Mayfield]] began the season driving for the team after competing in several races in their No. 66 car in late 2007. After falling out of the Top 35 in Owner’s Points following the seventh race, Mayfield and Haas CNC split. 43 | colspan="14" | |} == Busch Series == === Car No. 00 history === ; Jason Leffler (2003–2004) The Haas team debuted in the [[2003 NASCAR Busch Series|2003 season]] with the No. 00 Haas Automation Chevrolet. [[Troy Cline]] attempted four races, failing to qualify twice before making the field at [[Auto Club Speedway|Fontana]] using [[Aramendia Motorsports]]’ No. 79 owner points.{{cite news |date=April 26, 2003 |title=BUSCH: Fontana starting lineup |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-fontana-starting-lineup/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220153242/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-fontana-starting-lineup/ |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=11 December 2016 |work=[[Motorsport.com]]}} [[Jason Leffler]] took over for the final four races, debuting at [[Kansas Speedway|Kansas]] with an 11th-place start and 16th-place finish despite a wreck. He followed with 11th-place finishes at [[Charlotte Motor Speedway|Charlotte]] and [[Phoenix Raceway|Phoenix]], then earned his first top-five by finishing 4th after starting 14th. The team went full-time in [[2004 NASCAR Busch Series|2004]]. After a slow start, Leffler had just two finishes outside the top 15—a 34th at California and a 17th at [[Bristol Motor Speedway|Bristol]]. He also earned a pole at California and scored his and Haas’ first win at [[Nashville Superspeedway|Nashville]].{{cite news |last1=Chemris |first1=Thomas |date=June 13, 2004 |title=USCH: Leffler wins first race at Nashville |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-leffler-wins-first-race-at-nashville/?s=1&q=jason+leffler+haas |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220165532/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-leffler-wins-first-race-at-nashville/?s=1&q=jason+leffler+haas |archive-date=20 December 2016 |access-date=17 December 2016 |work=[[Motorsport.com]]}} Leffler signed with [[Joe Gibbs Racing]] for a Cup ride in 2005 and was released from Haas CNC before the end of 2004.{{cite news |author1=Morris News Service |author1-link=Morris News Service |date=October 9, 2004 |title='Front Row Joe' posts his second consecutive pole |url=http://chronicle.augusta.com/stories/2004/10/09/nas_430798.shtml#.WKNEyTsrKUk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215023134/http://chronicle.augusta.com/stories/2004/10/09/nas_430798.shtml#.WKNEyTsrKUk |archive-date=15 February 2017 |access-date=14 February 2017 |work=[[The Augusta Chronicle]] |location=[[Kansas City, Kansas]]}} Hendrick development driver [[Blake Feese]] replaced him, starting seventh at Kansas, but struggled in all four of his starts. As Feese faltered, Haas continued to search for a driver and promoted crew chief [[Bootie Barker]] to the Cup program. [[Tony Raines]] finished tenth at Phoenix, and [[Justin Labonte]] drove the remaining races. ; Justin Labonte (2005) In 2005, [[Justin Labonte]] drove full-time in the newly renumbered No. 44 [[U.S. Coast Guard]] Chevy for '''Labonte-Haas Motorsports''', a merger between Haas CNC and [[Labonte Motorsports]].{{cite web |date=February 4, 2005 |title=BUSCH: Labonte-Haas Motorsports adds sponsor |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-labonte-haas-motorsports-adds-sponsor/?v=2&s=1&q=Justin+Labonte |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427143726/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-labonte-haas-motorsports-adds-sponsor/?v=2&s=1&q=Justin+Labonte |archive-date=27 April 2015 |access-date=20 April 2015 |website=motorsport.com |location=[[Harrisburg, North Carolina]]}} He had limited success, with a best finish of 7th at Talladega and 10th at Charlotte. After finishing 17th in points, he was released at season’s end. The No. 44, a Labonte family number, was not fielded by Haas again. ; Johnny Sauter (2006) In 2006, [[Johnny Sauter]] was hired to drive the No. 00 car, sponsored by [[Yellow Transportation]].{{cite web |author1=NASCAR |author1-link=NASCAR |date=January 21, 2006 |title=BUSCH: Daytona Preseason Thunder, day 11 report |url=http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-daytona-preseason-thunder-day-11-report/?v=2&s=1&q=johnny+sauter+2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427143719/http://www.motorsport.com/nascar-xs/news/busch-daytona-preseason-thunder-day-11-report/?v=2&s=1&q=johnny+sauter+2006 |archive-date=27 April 2015 |access-date=20 April 2015 |website=motorsport.com |location=[[Daytona Beach, Florida]]}} After finishing 8th in the Busch Series standings, the team moved up to the Cup Series as the No. 70. Haas CNC Racing was an American professional stock car racing team that competed in the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series and NASCAR Busch Series. Founded in 2002 by Gene Haas, the founder of Haas Automation, the team was established after Haas—then a sponsor of Hendrick Motorsports—decided to start his own operation. The team ceased operations after the 2008 season, merging into Stewart–Haas Racing when three-time NASCAR champion Tony Stewart joined as a driver and acquired a 50% ownership stake.
The team was based and headquartered in Kannapolis, North Carolina – roughly 10 miles (16 km) north of Charlotte Motor Speedway – alongside sister team and Formula One entrant Haas F1 Team.
